AI FEATURE USABILITY STUDY 2026

Modeling Misclick Changes Across the Roadmap

Estimating design impact across iterations to assess launch readiness, spark design improvements, and reinforce confidence in the product’s winning qualities.

The product demonstrated strong task effectiveness but weak path efficiency. Benchmarked design comparisons show meaningful reductions.

The Pilot launch experience models meaningful usability improvement. Product leadership determines whether the available evidence, technical readiness, and remaining uncertainty are acceptable for launch.*

The roadmap models a 54.6% reduction, but the remaining 682 is not a backlog of known defects. It is the modeled remainder after the Pilot recommendations.

Why the model does not assume 100%: The recommendations are intended to remove the systematic friction identified in the study, but not every recorded misclick can be attributed to a specific design issue. The tested design comparisons reduced misclicks by 38.0% to 81.4%, averaging 59.0%. The model applies that observed average to recommendations without a direct comparison rather than assuming they eliminate all associated misclicks. This is a conservative evidence boundary, not the design team’s performance target.

The remaining misclicks may include:

  • Residual friction that still existed in the better tested variants
  • Misclicks caused by multiple issues within the same task
  • User exploration, especially when learning an unfamiliar AI workflow
  • Individual variation in how participants interpreted the task
  • Issues not isolated by the study’s task-level data
  • New or different friction that could appear when all changes are integrated

Evidence-based next step: Re-test the integrated Pilot with the same tasks and metrics, locate where residual misclicks concentrate, then prioritize the next design cycle by frequency, severity, and impact on critical-task success and recovery.

Tested comparisons quantify observed differences. For recommendations without a direct comparison benchmark, the model applies the average 59.0% reduction observed across the three benchmarked design comparisons. The benchmarked reductions were 57.6%, 38.0%, and 81.4%; their visible rounded average is 59.0%. Estimated values are directional and are not measured post-change performance. Reliably determining realized savings and launch readiness requires testing the integrated updated product.

* Industry standards define what to evaluate, but do not prescribe a universal acceptable misclick count or percentage. Targets should be set by the product team based on task, risk, and a repeatable benchmark.

ISO 9241-11Evaluate usability in context through effectiveness, efficiency, and satisfaction. Misclicks primarily inform efficiency; launch assessment should also consider task success and user confidence.Source
ISO/IEC 25010Consider operability, user-error protection, self-descriptiveness, reliability, and recoverability.Source
WCAG 2.2Evaluate accessibility through testable criteria organized around perceivable, operable, understandable, and robust experiences.Source
Task success referenceIndustry reference: approximately 78% average task completion across 1,189 tasks in 115 studies. This study: 91.3% overall mission completion across 230 of 252 attempts, with individual flows ranging from 86% to 100%. Among 219 successful attempts with retained misclick metrics, 19.6% were direct successes with zero misclicks and 80.4% were indirect successes with one or more misclicks. Because the study was unmoderated and the prototype accepted only the correct CTA, indirect success means participants independently recovered after an incorrect interaction.
Study 91.3% | Reference 78% | +13.3 percentage points
Source
UMUX-Lite referenceIndustry reference: the established SUS average is 68. This study: mean UMUX-Lite was 80.6 of 100; the published regression gives an estimated SUS-equivalent of 75.3, above average and within the published “Excellent” range of 72.76 to 85.58. The 75.3 value is an estimated SUS-equivalent, not an administered 10-item SUS score.
Estimated SUS-equivalent 75.3 | Average 68 | +7.3 points
Source
Misclick and error ratesIndustry standard: no universal acceptable misclick percentage. Lower is better; targets depend on task stakes, error opportunities, and recoverability. This study: 19.6% direct, zero-misclick success among successful attempts with retained metrics. No universal misclick threshold exists. Lower is better; critical workflows should approach zero serious or unrecoverable errors, while lower-risk exploratory tasks may tolerate some recoverable misclicks. 80.4% included at least one misclick.
Design goal: increase direct success; zero serious errors in critical workflows
Source
